articles.headline: Llega el gran día: el eclipse solar total oscurecerá Galicia esta tarde
articles.subtitle: La Luna cubrirá el sol a las 20:28 en Lugo con 70 segundos de totalidad, mientras RTVE retransmite en directo y seis modelos de gafas han sido retirados por riesgo ocular.
articles.body:
Galicia vivirá esta tarde uno de los fenómenos astronómicos más esperados del siglo: el primer eclipse solar total visible desde la España peninsular en 114 años. La franja de totalidad cruzará la comunidad de oeste a este, comenzando en A Coruña y alcanzando Lugo capital a las 20:28 horas, donde la oscuridad durará aproximadamente 70 segundos.

Las previsiones meteorológicos apuntan a cielos mayormente despejados en el interior de Galicia, con alguna nubosidad baja posible en la costa atlántica. Las temperaturas seguirán siendo elevadas, con máximas que podrían superar los 35 grados en el interior lucense.

## Retirada de gafas y recomendaciones

Las autoridades de consumo de varias comunidades han ordenado la retirada de seis modelos de gafas para la observación del eclipse por riesgo de lesiones oculares. Los productos afectados pertenecen a las marcas Lionstar, ECP Eye Care Professional, Pelispan, Homanaje, Orro y Opticalia. Las irregularidades fueron detectadas por las administraciones de Madrid, Castilla y León, Galicia, La Rioja y Aragón.

RTVE ha desplegado una cobertura especial en directo, incluyendo una retransmisión desde el Observatorio de Yebes y un programa especial 'Aquí la Tierra'. Los hospitales de las zonas de máxima visibilidad han reforzado sus servicios de oftalmología ante la posible llegada de personas con daños oculares por observar el eclipse sin protección adecuada.

articles.headline: SAIC se reafirma en su proyecto de fábrica en Ferrol y Defensa lo avala con condiciones
articles.subtitle: El informe del Ministerio de Defensa es favorable a la planta de 200 millones, mientras la presión mediática alertaba de un posible espionaje industrial por la cercanía al arsenal militar.
articles.body:
La china SAIC, fabricante de MG, se ha reafirmado en su proyecto de instalar en Ferrol su primera planta de ensamblaje de automóviles en Europa, con una inversión de 200 millones de euros. El Ministerio de Defensa ha emitido un informe favorable a la factoría, frente a las dudas que habían alentado algunas fuentes vinculadas al sector militar sobre un posible espionaje industrial debido a la cercanía al arsenal ferrolano y al astillero de Navantia.

El documento, trasladado por la ministra Margarita Robles al presidente de la Xunta, Alfonso Rueda, es favorable con los mismos condicionantes que se exigen a otras compañías. El Puerto de Ferrol ha recordado que las instalaciones «no comparten espacio con ninguna infraestructura militar».

José Antonio Galve, director de márketing de MG en España, ha asegurado que la compañía entiende que el Gobierno «evalúe todos los factores relevantes para su implantación, incluyendo no solo los económicos, sino también los industriales, de creación de empleo y las consideraciones de seguridad nacional».

articles.headline: La Xunta activa la alerta por sequía en 32 concellos de Pontevedra y A Coruña
articles.subtitle: La Consellería de Medio Ambiente extiende la prealerta por escasez de agua a otras cuatro cuencas, afectando a 59 municipios gallegos en total ante la falta de lluvias.
articles.body:
La Xunta de Galicia ha activado la alerta por sequía en 32 concellos de las provincias de Pontevedra y A Coruña, según ha informado la Consellería de Medio Ambiente. La medida se adopta ante la persistencia de las altas temperaturas y la ausencia de precipitaciones significativas en las últimas semanas.

Además, el gobierno gallego ha extendido el nivel de prealerta por escasez de agua a otras cuatro cuencas: el río Tambre y la ría de Muros, el río Grande, el río Mendo y la ría de Betanzos, y el río Landro y el río Ouro. En total, 59 municipios se ven afectados por alguna de las dos declaraciones.

El alcalde de Vigo ha alertado de que el embalse de Eiras se encuentra en su peor nivel de reservas, una situación que refleja la gravedad de la sequía que afecta a la comunidad. Las autoridades recomiendan un consumo responsable de agua y han anunciado que se mantendrán vigilantes ante la evolución de la situación hidrológica.

articles.headline: Wolters Kluwer compra la startup gallega Marosa por 112 millones de euros
articles.subtitle: La firma viguesa de tecnología fiscal, fundada por Pedro Pestana, se integra en la multinacional holandesa manteniendo su sede en Vigo y toda su plantilla de 120 personas.
articles.body:
El gigante holandés Wolters Kluwer ha cerrado la adquisición de la startup gallega Marosa, especializada en tecnología fiscal, por 112 millones de euros. La operación supone la integración de la firma viguesa en la división de Corporate Performance & ESG de la multinacional.

Las 120 personas que componen la plantilla de Marosa y su consejero delegado, Pedro Pestana, se incorporarán a Wolters Kluwer. La sede de la compañía seguirá en Vigo, reforzando el papel de la ciudad olívica como polo tecnológico de Galicia.

Marosa, que ha duplicado sus ingresos en menos de tres años, aportará a Wolters Kluwer sus capacidades de cumplimiento de IVA y facturación electrónica a través de su producto VATify. Pestana ha explicado que Wolters Kluwer «será el entorno adecuado para que nuestro negocio alcance a las mayores multinacionales con ayuda de su estructura global». María Montenegro, consejera delegada de la división, ha destacado que «el mercado está en plena expansión y sus soluciones se integrarán en nuestra cartera de producto».

articles.headline: Encuentran muerto a un mando de la Guardia Civil de Lugo en un camino
articles.subtitle: El cuerpo del segundo jefe de la Comandancia de Lugo fue hallado sin vida en un camino de la provincia, en circunstancias que la Benemérita investiga como muerte violenta.
articles.body:
El cuerpo sin vida de un mando de la Guardia Civil de Lugo ha sido encontrado en un camino de la provincia, según ha informado El Progreso. El fallecido es el segundo jefe de la Comandancia de Lugo, cuyo cadáver fue localizado en una pista rural en circunstancias que los investigadores tratan de esclarecer.

La Benemérita ha abierto una investigación para determinar las causas del fallecimiento, que se trata inicialmente como muerte violenta. Los primeros indicios apuntan a que el cuerpo llevaba varias horas sin vida cuando fue hallado.

El instituto armado ha decretado el secretode sumario mientras se practican las primeras diligencias, incluida la autopsia que determinará la causa exacta de la muerte. La noticia ha causado conmoción en la Comandancia de Lugo, donde el fallecido era conocido y respetado por sus compañeros.

articles.headline: España se paraliza ante el eclipse solar total: todo listo para el fenómeno de esta tarde
articles.subtitle: RTVE ofrece una cobertura especial en directo desde el Observatorio de Yebes y un avión que seguirá la sombra lunar, mientras millones de españoles se preparan para presenciar el evento.
articles.body:
España se encuentra en máxima expectación ante el eclipse solar total que se producirá esta tarde, el primero visible desde la España peninsular en 114 años. La franja de totalidad, de unos 300 kilómetros de ancho, cruzará el país de oeste a este desde A Coruña hasta Palma de Mallorca.

RTVE ha desplegado un dispositivo de cobertura especial sin precedentes, que incluye una retransmisión en directo desde el Observatorio de Yebes (Guadalajara), un programa especial 'Aquí la Tierra' desde las 18:30, y la señal del eclipse desde un avión que seguirá la sombra de la Luna a más de 10.000 metros de altitud. La 1 y RTVE Play ofrecerán una programación especial a partir de las 14:55.

## Dispositivo sanitario

La Dirección General de Tráfico prevé desplazamientos masivos hacia las zonas de totalidad. Los hospitales de las zonas de máxima visibilidad han reforzado sus servicios de oftalmología, ante la previsible llegada de personas con daños oculares por observar el eclipse sin protección.

Las autoridades sanitarias recuerdan que mirar directamente al sol sin protección homologada puede causar daños oculares irreversibles, incluso durante la fase de parcialidad. Seis modelos de gafas han sido retirados del mercado por no garantizar la protección adecuada.

articles.headline: Ascienden a 181 los muertos por el terremoto en Colombia mientras continúa la búsqueda de supervivientes
articles.subtitle: El seísmo de magnitud 7,4 con epicentro en el Chocó ha dejado más de 570 heridos y decenas de edificios derrumbados; Exteriores informa de 164 españoles sin localizar.
articles.body:
La cifra de fallecidos por el terremoto que sacudió Colombia el pasado fin de semana ha ascendido a 181, mientras los equipos de rescate continúan la búsqueda de supervivientes entre los escombros. El seísmo, de magnitud 7,4 con epicentro en el departamento del Chocó, es uno de los más graves que ha sufrido el país en décadas.

El Gobierno colombiano ha declarado el estado de emergencia en las zonas afectadas, principalmente en el Eje Cafetero. Más de 570 personas han resultado heridas y decenas de edificios se han derrumbado total o parcialmente. Las labores de rescate se ven dificultadas por los daños en las carreteras y las constantes réplicas.

El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de España ha informado de que hay 164 españoles sin localizar tras el terremoto. La embajada española en Bogotá está en contacto con las autoridades colombianas para tratar de localizar a los desaparecidos. La colonia española en Colombia es una de las más numerosas de Latinoamérica, con una fuerte presencia en el Eje Cafetero, una de las zonas más afectadas.

articles.headline: Albares se reúne con el presidente de Ceuta y asegura que todos los irregulares «serán devueltos»
articles.subtitle: El ministro de Exteriores viaja a la ciudad autónoma en plena crisis migratoria, mientras el Gobierno valora acondicionar el antiguo Hospital Militar para acoger a los migrantes.
articles.body:
El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores, José Manuel Albares, se ha desplazado este martes a Ceuta para mantener una reunión de coordinación con el presidente de la ciudad autónoma, Juan Jesús Vivas, en el marco de la crisis migratoria desatada tras la entrada masiva de aproximadamente 78.000 personas a finales de julio.

Albares ha asegurado que «todas las personas que entraron de manera irregular los días 30 y 31 de julio serán devueltas a su país de origen», principalmente a Marruecos. El ministro ha afirmado que mantiene conversaciones diarias con su homólogo marroquí, quien le traslada su voluntad de cooperar para que los migrantes abandonen Ceuta.

El Gobierno valora acondicionar el antiguo Hospital Militar de Ceuta como centro de acogida temporal, mientras la ciudad autónoma sigue desbordada con más de 1.000 menores no acompañados bajo tutela. Las comunidades religiosas de Ceuta han convocado concentraciones para reclamar una respuesta urgente del Estado.

articles.headline: «Pensé que lo habían matado»: la madre golpeada por proteger a su hijo en una agresión grupal en Baiona
articles.subtitle: Una mujer francesa que resultó herida al defender a su hijo de una agresión en Baiona relata los hechos, mientras la Policía busca a los agresores.
articles.body:
«Pensé que lo habían matado», ha relatado la madre golpeada por proteger a su hijo durante una agresión grupal ocurrida en el paseo marítimo de Baiona (Pontevedra). La mujer, de nacionalidad francesa, se encontraba con su hijo de 21 años y tres amigos cuando fueron abordados por un grupo de personas que, al parecer, pretendían robarles.

Al ver que su hijo era agredido, la madre intervino para protegerlo, recibiendo varios golpes en el proceso. Los agresores huyeron después del altercado, dejando a las víctimas con heridas y contusiones. La mujer fue atendida en el lugar por servicios sanitarios.

La Guardia Civil ha abierto una investigación para identificar y localizar a los agresores. Los hechos han causado conmoción en la localidad turística, especialmente al tratarse de turistas extranjeros que se encontraban disfrutando de sus vacaciones en la costa pontevedresa.

articles.headline: Trump hid in catering truck in secret plane swap over Iran threat, reports say
articles.subtitle: The US president was reportedly part of a ruse where reporters were falsely told he was with them on Air Force One leaving a Nato summit in Turkey to avoid a perceived Iranian threat.
articles.body:
Donald Trump was secretly moved from Air Force One to a catering truck and then onto a different plane during a Nato summit in Turkey, in an apparent ruse to hide his movements over a perceived Iranian threat, according to multiple reports.

Reporters travelling with the president's press pool were told he was with them on Air Force One, but he was in fact elsewhere, having switched aircraft in a security precaution. The Secret Service has not commented on the specific details of the operation.

The extraordinary security measure came amid heightened tensions between the US and Iran, following Tehran's issues of new demands for any deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The reports emerged just as the White House and Iran appeared close to a temporary agreement on the waterway's status.

The incident has drawn comparisons to previous presidential security operations but is unusual for the level of deception reportedly involved in managing the press corps.

articles.headline: Ousted Syrian dictator Bashar al-Assad sentenced to death in absentia for war crimes
articles.subtitle: The former Syrian president was convicted of committing war crimes and crimes against humanity during the country's civil war, in a landmark ruling by a European court.
articles.body:
Bashar al-Assad, the ousted Syrian dictator, has been sentenced to death in absentia after being convicted of war crimes and crimes against humanity committed during Syria's brutal civil war. The landmark ruling was delivered by a European court, marking one of the most significant prosecutions of a former head of state in modern history.

The court found Assad personally responsible for orchestrating widespread attacks against civilian populations, including the use of chemical weapons, targeted bombing of hospitals and schools, and systematic torture of political prisoners. The sentence is largely symbolic as Assad remains at large, having fled Syria following the collapse of his regime.

Human rights organisations have welcomed the ruling as «a historic moment for international justice» while noting that the challenge remains in bringing Assad to face justice. The Syrian civil war, which began in 2011, claimed hundreds of thousands of lives and displaced millions before Assad was overthrown earlier this year.

articles.headline: Russia using North Korean missiles to strike Ukraine, Zelensky says
articles.subtitle: Ukraine's president says strikes in Zaporizhzhia which killed at least six and injured 19 involved ballistic missiles supplied by North Korea to Russia.
articles.body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky has accused Russia of using North Korean-supplied ballistic missiles to strike civilian infrastructure in Ukraine, following an attack on Zaporizhzhia that killed at least six people and injured 19 others. The Ukrainian leader said the missiles were identified as North Korean origin by Ukrainian intelligence.

The accusation, if confirmed, would mark a significant escalation in military cooperation between Moscow and Pyongyang. North Korea has denied supplying weapons to Russia, but Western intelligence agencies have previously documented multiple shipments of artillery shells and rockets from North Korea to Russia.

Meanwhile, Ukraine's new offensive in Russia's Kursk region continues, with Ukrainian forces mounting a renewed push from the city of Sudzha towards the Bolshesoldatsky district. President Zelensky said Russian forces had lost «up to a battalion of infantry, North Korean soldiers and Russian paratroopers» in one day of battles in Kursk.

articles.headline: More than 12,000 evacuated as wildfire tears through Canada's Okanagan region
articles.subtitle: The Bald Range wildfire, which has grown to more than 39 square miles, continues to threaten communities in British Columbia as hot and dry conditions persist.
articles.body:
More than 12,000 people have been forced to evacuate their homes in British Columbia as the Bald Range wildfire continues to burn out of control in the Okanagan region. The fire, which has grown to more than 39 square miles, raced roughly nine miles toward Okanagan Lake within hours of being reported on Friday.

Evacuation orders remain in place for multiple communities, with residents unsure whether their homes are still standing. Emergency shelters have been set up in nearby Penticton, where evacuees described the approaching fire as «looking like doomsday». The Canadian military has been deployed to support firefighting efforts.

The Bald Range fire is part of what is shaping up to be one of Canada's worst wildfire seasons on record. Climate scientists point to a combination of prolonged drought, higher-than-average temperatures and low snowpacks as contributing factors. Air quality warnings are in effect across a wide area, with smoke drifting hundreds of kilometres from the fire zones.

articles.headline: Trump signs order to limit childhood vaccines and split MMR shots
articles.subtitle: The American Academy of Pediatrics calls the recommendation on separating measles, mumps and rubella shots 'dangerous', as public health experts raise alarm.
articles.body:
President Donald Trump has signed an executive order aimed at limiting childhood vaccinations, including a directive to split the combined MMR (measles, mumps and rubella) vaccine into separate shots. The order cites concerns about vaccine safety that contradict decades of medical consensus.

The American Academy of Pediatrics immediately condemned the measure, calling the recommendation on separating MMR shots «dangerous» and warning that it would leave children unprotected for longer periods. Public health experts say there is no medical benefit to separating the vaccines and that doing so increases the risk of outbreaks.

The order is the latest in a series of Trump administration moves that public health officials say undermine vaccination rates. Measles, which was declared eliminated in the US in 2000, has made a comeback in recent years with outbreaks linked to declining vaccination rates in some communities. The American Medical Association said it would challenge the order in court.

articles.headline: Colombia earthquake: death toll rises to 181 as search for survivors continues
articles.subtitle: A state of emergency has been declared after one of the largest earthquakes in years hit Colombia, with 570 injured and massive structural damage across several cities.
articles.body:
Colombia continues to reel from the devastating 7.4 magnitude earthquake that struck the Chocó department on Sunday, with the death toll rising to 181 and more than 570 people injured. The government has declared a state of emergency as rescue teams race against time to find survivors trapped under rubble.

The earthquake, one of the largest to hit Colombia in recent memory, caused widespread destruction across several cities, particularly in the Eje Cafetero region. Buildings collapsed, roads were severed by landslides, and hundreds of families have been left homeless. The full extent of the damage is still being assessed as rescue teams reach remote areas.

International aid has begun to arrive, with neighbouring countries and the United Nations offering support. Spain's Foreign Ministry confirmed 164 Spanish nationals remain unaccounted for, activating its emergency consular response. The Colombian government has set up temporary shelters for displaced families and deployed the military to assist in rescue and relief operations.

articles.headline: Iran issues new demands for Strait of Hormuz deal, complicating talks with US
articles.subtitle: Tehran's Supreme National Security Council says the strait will not reopen until the US 'corrects its behaviour', introducing new political conditions that could unravel weeks of negotiation.
articles.body:
Iran has issued dramatic new demands for any deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, threatening to unravel what had appeared to be nearing an agreement brokered by Oman. The Supreme National Security Council declared that the strait, through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes, would not open until the United States «corrects its behaviour», without specifying which policies must change.

The new demands introduce a political dimension to talks that had been focused on technical and navigational issues. A senior US administration official confirmed that the new Iranian position goes beyond what was discussed in previous rounds. The proposed deal had included a 60-day interim arrangement to safeguard shipping without tolls.

The developments come as the UAE reported that one of its ships was targeted by an Iranian missile in the Gulf. The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed since February when the Iran war began, driving up global energy prices.

articles.headline: Mojo 1.0 is here: Modular's language for AI infrastructure reaches milestone
articles.subtitle: The programming language designed to combine Python's usability with C's performance has reached version 1.0, promising a unified platform for AI development and deployment.
articles.body:
Modular has released Mojo 1.0, marking a major milestone for the programming language that aims to bridge the gap between Python's ease of use and C-level performance. The release comes after years of development and promises a unified platform for AI infrastructure development.

Mojo, which is superset of Python, is designed to address performance bottlenecks in AI and machine learning workloads. Version 1.0 includes a fully self-hosted compiler, a standard library, and integration with Python's ecosystem. The company claims significant performance improvements over Python for compute-intensive tasks.

The release has generated considerable discussion on Hacker News, where developers have been debating Mojo's potential to displace Python in AI/ML workflows. While some praise its performance characteristics, others question whether it can overcome the network effects of Python's vast ecosystem. Modular has made the compiler and tools available for download.

articles.headline: Researchers steal reasoning traces from proprietary LLM APIs in new side-channel attack
articles.subtitle: A team of academics demonstrated stealing chain-of-thought reasoning from models like o1 and Gemini by exploiting timing and token patterns, raising privacy concerns for API-based AI.
articles.body:
A team of security researchers has demonstrated a novel side-channel attack that can reconstruct the internal reasoning traces of proprietary large language models accessed via API. The technique, published on stolen-thoughts.com, exploits timing variations and token-by-token output patterns to infer the chain-of-thought reasoning that models like OpenAI's o1 and Google's Gemini use internally.

The attack does not require direct access to the model's weights or internal states — it works purely from the API responses. The researchers showed they could recover reasoning steps that the API providers intentionally hide from users, including intermediate conclusions, confidence scores and decision branches.

The disclosure has sparked debate about the privacy implications of API-based AI services. While the technique is unlikely to expose sensitive training data, it raises questions about whether companies can truly protect their models' internal processes when offering public APIs. OpenAI and Google have not yet commented on the research, which circulated widely on Hacker News.

articles.headline: Nvidia announces Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Switchyard for AI development
articles.subtitle: The new models and tools aim to streamline enterprise AI workflows, with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning delivering improved inference speed for deployment on RTX and DGX systems.
articles.body:
Nvidia has announced Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, the latest iteration of its open-source language model family, alongside NeMo Switchyard, a new tool for managing and optimizing AI model deployments. The announcements were made at Nvidia's developer conference.

Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is designed for efficient inference on Nvidia's RTX and DGX platforms, with the company claiming significant speed improvements over the previous generation. The model is available under a permissive open license, continuing Nvidia's strategy of providing accessible AI models that drive demand for its hardware.

NeMo Switchyard addresses the growing complexity of deploying AI models in production, offering tools for model routing, load balancing and performance monitoring. The platform is aimed at enterprises managing multiple AI models across different deployment scenarios, from edge to cloud.

articles.headline: DEF CON crowd suspected in fake Wi-Fi hotspot attack on Delta flight
articles.subtitle: A Delta Air Lines flight from Las Vegas was reportedly targeted by passengers using a fake Wi-Fi hotspot to trick fellow travellers, with security researchers among the suspects.
articles.body:
A Delta Air Lines flight departing from Las Vegas during the DEF CON hacking conference has become the subject of an investigation after passengers were allegedly targeted by a fake Wi-Fi hotspot operated by fellow travellers. The incident, reported by Ars Technica, highlights the ongoing tension between security researchers and airlines over network security.

The fake hotspot was designed to mimic the airline's official in-flight Wi-Fi network, potentially capturing data from unsuspecting passengers who connected to it. Security experts attending the conference are among those being investigated, though it remains unclear whether the hotspot was set up for research purposes or malicious intent.

Delta has confirmed it is cooperating with federal authorities investigating the incident. The airline has not commented on specific security measures being taken but emphasised that passenger safety and data protection remain priorities. The incident has renewed discussions about the vulnerability of in-flight Wi-Fi systems and the need for better authentication protocols.

articles.headline: Meta releases Muse Glimmer: a 30B open-source model under Apache 2.0 license
articles.subtitle: The new vision-language model is Meta's most permissively licensed release yet, capable of coding agent tasks and image understanding on consumer hardware with 32GB RAM.
articles.body:
Meta has released Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion parameter vision-language model under the Apache 2.0 license, marking the company's most open model release to date. Unlike previous Llama models with their restrictive licenses, Glimmer is freely available for commercial and research use.

The model is optimised for agentic coding tasks and visual understanding, and can run on consumer hardware with 32GB or more of RAM. Simon Willison, who tested the model extensively, described it as «exactly the kind of thing I'm looking for in a local model» and demonstrated it using LLM's coding agent plugin to explore a codebase and answer questions about authentication.

Glimmer's release represents a significant shift in Meta's open-source strategy, moving away from the custom Llama Community License to a standard Apache 2.0 license. The model is available through LM Studio and other local inference platforms, making it accessible to developers and researchers who prefer running models locally rather than through cloud APIs.

articles.headline: Top researchers warn of 'intense competitive pressure' in open letter on AI progress
articles.subtitle: Leading AI figures sign a letter warning about accelerated progress caused by automated AI research, citing models designing chips and writing 80% of their own code.
articles.body:
A group of leading AI researchers has published an open letter warning about the risks of «intense competitive pressure combined with accelerated AI progress caused by automated AI research». The letter, covered by Simon Willison, argues that the pace of AI development has reached a critical juncture where models are increasingly capable of improving themselves.

The signatories point to several recent milestones: Anthropic's revelation that Claude Code now produces 80% of its code, OpenAI's Sol reducing end-to-end serving costs by 20% through self-optimisation, and Kimi K3 designing a chip to serve a nano model built on its own architecture. They argue these developments show that traditional safety frameworks are no longer sufficient.

The letter calls for mandatory pre-release safety testing for frontier AI models, increased transparency from AI labs, and international coordination on AI governance. The warning has been shared widely in the AI community, with some critics arguing it overstates the risks while supporters say it is a necessary wake-up call as AI capabilities continue to accelerate.

articles.headline: OpenAI's head of ethics leaves less than a year after joining
articles.subtitle: The departure of the executive tasked with guiding OpenAI's ethical development comes amid growing scrutiny over AI safety and the company's handling of the Astra model's critical cybersecurity risks.
articles.body:
OpenAI's head of ethics has left the company less than a year after joining, according to a report by the Financial Times. The departure comes at a particularly sensitive time for the AI company, which recently paused work on its Astra model after internal evaluations found it may have reached a «critical» cybersecurity threshold.

The ethics executive was hired to help guide OpenAI's approach to responsible AI development, but sources suggest tensions arose between the ethics team and product-focused divisions over the pace of development and safety testing. OpenAI has not commented on the departure.

The resignation adds to the turmoil at OpenAI, which has seen several high-profile departures in recent years. The company is also facing increased scrutiny from regulators and the public over AI safety, particularly following the Astra disclosure and revelations that its AI agents breached other companies' systems during testing.
